For finite real scores, every softmax weight is strictly positive, so each output row uses the value row of every input position. This is one direct attention edge; composing $L$ layers yields at most one such edge per layer, hence at most $L$ attention edges independent of $n$.

First consider the compactly supported equivariant map. If $f=0$, the zero Transformer suffices. Otherwise its support $K$ is a nonempty compact permutation-invariant set. Compactness bounds all scalar entries of matrices in $K$; choose real $a<b$ with every entry in $[a,b]$. Since a nonzero continuous function is nonzero on an open set, $K$ has positive measure and the bounds can be chosen with $a<b$. The common affine map $T(X)=(X-a\mathbf1)/(b-a)$ sends $K$ into $[0,1]^{d\times n}$ and commutes with column permutations. A residual width-four ReLU sublayer implements $z\mapsto\alpha z+\beta$ on every feature by
$$
z+(\alpha-1)\bigl(\operatorname{ReLU}(z)-\operatorname{ReLU}(-z)\bigr)+\beta=\alpha z+\beta;
$$
two hidden units handle one feature and finitely many layers handle all $d$ features. Thus $T$ can be inserted in the Yun architecture.

Choose $\delta=1/m$ with integer $m$ large enough that $n\le\delta^{-d}$, the duplicate-cell bound below is small, and $M=\delta^{-nd}>d+1+\log(n)/\lambda$ for a fixed $\lambda>0$. Partition the normalized cube into half-open grid cells of side $\delta$. Their preimages under $T$ have side $h=(b-a)\delta$. By [F4], the oscillation of $f$ between two points of $K$ at distance at most $\sqrt{dn}\,h$ tends to zero with $\delta$. For each orbit of distinct-column grid matrices $L$ under column permutations, if the closed preimage cell meets $K$, choose one representative $X_L$ in that intersection and put $A(L)=f(X_L)$; transport the choice by permutations and set $A(L)=0$ on orbits whose cells miss $K$. This is a finite choice and gives $A(LP)=A(L)P$. Apply the first assertion of [F3] to this table.

The table network agrees with $f$ on every point of $K$ in a distinct-column cell up to the oscillation in step 1.2. The union of cells whose grid matrices have duplicate columns has measure at most
$$
\binom n2\,m^{d(n-1)}h^{dn}=\binom n2(b-a)^{dn}\delta^d,
$$
because for each pair of columns, equality leaves only $m^{d(n-1)}$ grid matrices. The table is zero on cells not meeting $K$; cells meeting $K$ but lying partly outside it are contained in the $\sqrt{dn}\,h$-neighborhood of $K$. Intersect these neighborhoods with one fixed bounded box containing $K$. Along any sequence $h_j\downarrow0$, the resulting closed neighborhoods decrease to $K$ and have finite measure; [F5]–[F6] imply that their excess measure over $K$ tends to zero. The table values are bounded because $f$ is continuous on compact $K$. Outside the normalized cube the sentinel branch of [F3] returns zero, as does $f$. Therefore the integrated $L_p$ error of the modified lookup tends to zero as $\delta\downarrow0$.

Now consider continuous $f$ on compact $K$ without symmetry. If $K$ has zero Lebesgue measure, the integral is zero for any network. Otherwise let $a,b$ be the minimum and maximum of its scalar entries; again $a<b$. Put $\alpha=(b-a)^{-1}$ and choose
$$
E_{rj}=(b-a)(j-1)-a\qquad(1\le r\le d,\ 1\le j\le n).
$$
The first residual width-four sublayers scale $X+E$ by $\alpha$, producing entries $(X_{rj}-a)/(b-a)+(j-1)$. Partition each normalized feature interval $[0,1]$ into grid intervals of width $\delta=1/m$. The resulting quantized matrices lie in $G_{\delta,\mathrm{pos}}$ from [F3], where position offsets make every column distinct. For each grid cell meeting $K$, choose a representative $X_L\in K$ and set $A(L)=f(X_L)$; set arbitrary values, for example zero, on cells disjoint from $K$. The position-tagged assertion of [F3] realizes this finite table exactly.

By [F4], for sufficiently small $\delta$ every point of $K$ and the representative in its grid cell have outputs within any prescribed tolerance. The cell diameter in the original coordinates is at most $\sqrt{dn}(b-a)\delta$, and $K$ has finite measure because it is compact and bounded. Thus the integrated $L_p(K)$ error of the modified position-tagged lookup can be made arbitrarily small.

It remains to replace the modified gates and uniform hardmax in [F3] by the standard ReLU and softmax of $\mathcal T^{2,1,4}$. For a three-piece scalar map
$$
\phi(t)=
\begin{cases}
b_1,&t<c_1,\\
a_2t+b_2,&c_1\le t<c_2,\\
a_3t+b_3,&t\ge c_2,
\end{cases}
$$
replace each jump by a linear ramp of width $\rho>0$. The resulting continuous piecewise-affine map is a sum of a constant and four ReLUs: its first two ReLU coefficients are $A_1=(a_2c_1+b_2-b_1)/\rho$ and $a_2-A_1$, and its last two are $A_2-a_2$ and $a_3-A_2$, where $A_2=(a_3c_2+b_3-a_2(c_2-\rho)-b_2)/\rho$. Direct substitution shows it agrees with $\phi$ outside the two ramp intervals. A width-four ReLU sublayer realizes this formula. For any finite score vector $s$, softmax of $\lambda s$ converges as $\lambda\to\infty$ to equal weights on its maximizing coordinates and zero elsewhere; hence it converges to the uniform hardmax used in [F3].

To control the unbounded input domain in the first assertion, insert an exact sentinel gate before simulating the lookup. For a quantized matrix $Z$, put $s_j=\sum_{r=1}^d Z_{rj}$ and
$$

$$

If all entries of $Z$ are in $[0,1]$, then every $s_j\ge0$, so every shifted entry is nonnegative. If any entry is the sentinel $-M$, then $\min_j s_j\le -M+d-1$. The entropy identity
$$

and the bounds $-\sum_jw_j\log w_j\le\log n$ and $\sum_je^{-\lambda s_j}\ge e^{-\lambda\min_j s_j}$ imply $\bar s\le\min_j s_j+(\log n)/\lambda<-1$, by the choice in step 1.2.
